test_title: PYST 02: SSC Stenographer 2025: General Awareness (Held On: 06 Aug, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: gk
question: At what orientation does a rotating coil in a uniform magnetic field generate the maximum induced EMF?

options.text: When the coil's plane is at 45° to the magnetic field lines
When the magnetic flux through the coil is maximum
When the coil's plane is perpendicular (90°) to the magnetic field lines
When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines

solution:
The correct answer is __**When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines​.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Induced EMF is given by Faraday’s law, which depends on the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil.
 
• **Magnetic flux is maximum when the coil’s plane is perpendicular to the field lines (flux change is zero here).**
 
• **EMF is maximum when the flux changes most rapidly, which occurs when the coil’s plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines**__ (flux = 0 but rate of change is maximum).
 
• At this orientation, every small rotation produces the greatest possible change in flux, resulting in maximum induced EMF.
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is – When the coil's plane is parallel to the magnetic field lines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Option (1): At 45°, some EMF is induced, but not maximum since the flux change rate is not the greatest.
 
• Option (2): When flux is maximum, EMF is zero because there is no change in flux at that instant.
 
• Option (3): When the coil’s plane is perpendicular, flux is maximum but EMF = 0 (same as above).
 
• Option (4): Correct, because maximum EMF is induced when flux = 0 and change of flux is maximum.
